notes.g01: Force arrows indicate the direction of load transfer, not its magnitude; actual practice varies greatly by period and region.
notes.g02: 「七铺作双抄双下昂」 (seven tiers, projecting outward twice and downward twice) is a term for the tier count and projection direction of a bracket set; it is not a count of individual components.
notes.g13: The Main Hall of Baoguo Temple is generally accepted as the only surviving Song-dynasty building that corroborates the relevant prescriptions of the Yingzao Fashi.
notes.g25: The multi-tenon and multi-socket components excavated at Hemudu are regarded as among the earliest known mortise-and-tenon examples in China.
notes.g31: The roof curve is a piecewise approximation rather than a true circular arc; in models it should be generated as a polyline, not a spline.
notes.g54: 「窑洞营造技艺」, the yaodong construction technique, is listed among China's national intangible cultural heritage; the methods used in northern Shaanxi and in Qingyang, Gansu differ.
notes.g59: 「中国木拱桥传统营造技艺」, the traditional craft of building Chinese timber arch bridges, was transferred in December 2024 from the Urgent Safeguarding List to the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
